criteria_results.title: Prima facie case for BSA retaliation (31 U.S.C. § 5328) constructed
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum explicitly constructs all four elements of a prima facie BSA retaliation case under 31 U.S.C. § 5328. (1) Protected activity: The brief identifies Vasquez's April 3, 2023 internal memorandum to the CCO reporting suspected BSA/AML violations (layering through Orion Gateway) and her June 15, 2023 external report to FinCEN as protected activity. (2) Employer knowledge: Section V.A extensively argues that the Bank knew or believed Vasquez was the whistleblower, citing Hargrove's August 1 email naming her as the 'obvious candidate,' Caldwell's 'Let me handle this' reply, and Hargrove's statements to Prescott. The brief also invokes Staub/cat's paw liability and Heffernan for belief-based retaliation. (3) Adverse employment action: The termination on September 22, 2023 is clearly identified as the adverse action, along with the PIP as an intermediate adverse action. (4) Causal connection: The brief establishes causation through temporal proximity (PIP issued 13 days after Hargrove's email, termination 52 days later), the direct documentary evidence of retaliatory intent, the pretext evidence, and comparator evidence. The footnote also references the AMLA 2020 amendment to § 5323(g) protecting internal reporting. All prima facie elements are clearly articulated and supported with record evidence.
